identity.title: An intricate role of Ang II/AT1 in the modulation of monosodium glutamate-induced pulmonary fibrosis by TGF-beta/Smad through quercetin.

content.abstract: To investigate the protective actions of the natural flavonoid quercetin against monosodium glutamate (MSG)-induced pulmonary fibrosis in rats, the present study targets the modulation of the TGF-beta/Smad signaling pathway and the involvement of Ang II/AT1. The experimental model involved the treatment of rats with MSG (0.6 g/kg body weight) for 4 weeks and quercetin dosages of 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg/kg body weight. The study applied the combination of biochemical, molecular, and histopathological evaluation to identify the role of quercetin in impacting major cytokines (IL-17, IL-19, TGF-beta, VEGF), oxidative stress markers (TBARS, NO, SOD, CAT, GSH), extracellular matrix components (collagen-I, alpha-SMA, fibronectin), and fibrosis gene expression (TGF-beta1, Smad2/3/4, CTGF, Snail, Slug). MSG treatment increased pro-fibrotic cytokines, oxidative stress, and deposition of collagen in a significant amount, while administration of quercetin dose-dependently reversed the alterations. Quercetin also reversed the activity of antioxidant enzymes, reduced inflammatory cytokines, and inhibited TGF-beta/Smad signaling as indicated by lowered TGF-beta receptor II activation and following Smad phosphorylation. Molecular docking demonstrated that quercetin competitively binds to TGF-beta receptor II to inhibit MSG-induced fibrotic signaling. Quercetin inhibits MSG-induced lung fibrosis by inhibiting collagen accumulation and inflammatory cell invasion and has the potential to produce therapeutic effects by modulating TGF-beta/Smad signaling and restoring lung tissue homeostasis.
